evidence.quote: let renewable (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : Result<unit, LendingError> =
match Loans.renewable today loan library with
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The renewability guard (overdue, then limit, then holds, in the decision's order) is pulled out into one Tier 2 function, `Loans.renewable`. `Loans.renew` and the new Tier 2 `Loans.renewAll` both use it. The Tier 3 views ask `Loans.renewable` and only turn its LendingError result into display text (`renewalRefusal`). The CLI used to call Loans.renew and do the store load and save itself; it now calls Tier 3 use cases and stays presentation only. No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code re-decides renewability.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added in Tier 1 or 2: `renewable` and `renewAll` are pure and take `today` and `library` as arguments. Tier 3 reads today's date through the Clock port, and persists through the existing `commit` path, which uses the Store port. The CLI renew branch that called `ports.Store.Load` and `Save` directly and re-entered `Loans.renew` (an existing ARC-BND-02 problem) is replaced with a use-case call, which removes the problem without adding a new one.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The renewal limit is defined once, in `Policy.renewLimit`, and both the guard and the view refer to it. The refusal text takes the limit from the `RenewLimitReached` error and copies no literal. The guard order is written once, in `renewable`, and `loans`, `renew` and `renew-all` all use it, so their reasons cannot disagree.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rule is decided in Tier 2: `renewable` looks up the borrower and uses `Policy.renewLimit borrower.Type`. Tier 3 then works out "which limit applies to this loan" a second time: the renew use case looks up the borrower itself, and `Views.ofRenewal` applies `Policy.renewLimit` to that member's type (and `ofRenewAll` passes in the listed member). The two derivations agree, but the rule "the limit is the borrower's member type's" is re-derived in Tier 3 rather than taken from a Tier 2 result. That is a duplicated local derivation that does not contradict Tier 2.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effects are added. The borrower lookup in Tier 2 and Tier 3 is a pure read of the in-memory Library value. Persistence still goes through the existing `commit` and Store port.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The per-type limits (standard 2, student 1, staff 4) are defined once, in `Policy.renewLimit`, and both the Tier 2 guard and the Tier 3 view call that one function. The old single constant is replaced, not kept beside the new definition. No literal is copied. The lookup of the borrower happens twice, but that duplicated rule is scored under ARC-REV-01. The limit values themselves have one definition.
